title: Cosmos-PLV
body:
Which robot-learning checkpoint should I evaluate next, and why?
Nebius x NVIDIA Global AI Hackathon 2026 - Physical AI track

Dashboard clips are real screen recordings of the running application
(live metric script, live Cosmos3-Edge, live Nebius call); speed-ups are labelled.

caption: Problem: offline losses do not tell checkpoints apart, and every closed-loop rollout costs robot time. 93 retrained Diffusion Policy checkpoints, 4,650 simulator rollouts.
Pipeline: cheap PLV screening -> real robosuite rollouts -> NVIDIA Cosmos3-Edge (local GPU) + NVIDIA Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL served by Nebius Token Factory.
Live dashboard: the recommendation keeps the cheap-metric top 30% and ranks them by VLM-judged success. Verified success is shown only as a check.
Cheap screening runs the ORIGINAL PLV script on this checkpoint (Action L1, open-loop smoothness) - live, 2.5x speed.

labels: epoch 100: picks and places (sim label: success)
caption: Real simulator rollouts recorded by the pipeline (robosuite / MuJoCo, 10 fps, 2x speed) with privileged labels used only as ground truth.
Rollout viewer: real episode video, verified simulator outcome, and Cosmos3-Edge's per-keyframe answers to the task-free question 'where is the can?'.
Live: NVIDIA Cosmos3-Edge runs on the local RTX 3090 (load + 8 keyframes, 2x speed). A fixed rule turns visual states into grasp / drop / success.
Live: the same episode is sent to NVIDIA Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL on Nebius Token Factory - request id, latency and tokens are logged as evidence.
Results on 330 real rollouts: Nemotron judges success with 0.964 accuracy, Cosmos3-Edge 0.918. Failure TYPES are not solved (below a majority baseline).
Measured cost: about 2-3 s per episode per judge. The 772 Nebius calls of the main pipeline cost about $0.87 at the catalog price (about $3 including all exploratory studies).

title: What we learned (honest results)
body:
+ NVIDIA VLMs can replace a privileged success detector: 0.92-0.96 accuracy from video alone.
+ Adaptive rollout allocation needs 2-3x fewer rollouts; a time cut saves 16-20% robot time.
- In our short runs no PLV metric beats the free 'later epoch' baseline (rho 0.76-0.80 vs 0.82).
- Action-conditioned Cosmos world-model feedback is blocked: no faithful action adapter.
Models: nvidia/Cosmos3-Edge (local), nvidia/Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL (Nebius Token Factory).
